text: The degree-p piece consists of finitely supported families whose i-th entry lies in Gᵢ(p), exactly the direct-sum grading in [Hazrat §1.2.6](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=24). Swapping the summand and degree indices proves the internal decomposition. The index family may be infinite or empty; each element still has finite support. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/DirectSum.lean#L209) passes.
Each degree-p piece has exactly componentwise degree-p membership.
A homogeneous element inserted into one summand keeps its degree.

The value is the range of the componentwise subtype inclusion, so it contains exactly finitely supported homogeneous families of the fixed degree p. This realizes [Hazrat §1.2.6](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=24)’s direct sum of degree-p pieces inside the total direct sum. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/DirectSum.lean#L209) passes.
Range membership is equivalent to degree-p membership in every component.

Rearranging ⨁p⨁i Gᵢ(p) as ⨁i⨁p Gᵢ(p), then recomposing each internal grading, gives a linear equivalence with ⨁i Mᵢ. The source checks that it is the canonical inclusion on every generator. This establishes both spanning and independence for [Hazrat §1.2.6](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=24)’s grading, without finiteness of i. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/DirectSum.lean#L85) passes.
The inverse of each piece equivalence retains the original components.
Recomposition agrees with canonical summand inclusion on generators.

The bundled grading uses directSumPiece as its piece field, so the equation is definitional. That submodule is a range of [Mathlib’s direct-sum map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249) applied to the piece inclusions; it retains the fixed degree p rather than adding the summand index to it. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/DirectSum.lean#L209) passes.
The selected piece has the intended componentwise membership criterion.

The included element has its degree-p entry at i and zero elsewhere, and every piece contains zero. Hence it belongs to the componentwise degree-p submodule. This is the generator behavior of [Mathlib’s direct-sum map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249); DecidableEq supports the displayed summand insertion. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/DirectSum.lean#L62) passes.
The homogeneous inclusion agrees with the ambient summand insertion.

Expand each input into its finite homogeneous decomposition and apply multilinearity in the finitely many slots. Agreement on every homogeneous tuple then gives agreement everywhere. The source uses the diagonal submodule, so subtraction is unnecessary; the semiring scope matches [Mathlib’s dfinsuppFamily](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Multilinear/DFinsupp.lean#L91). The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Multilinear/Basic.lean#L112) passes.
Restricting a total map to homogeneous pieces and extending recovers that map.

The componentwise inclusion is injective because each subtype inclusion is injective. LinearEquiv.ofInjective therefore identifies its domain with exactly its range, using [Mathlib’s direct-sum map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249). The forward and inverse formulas verify the same coordinates; the inverse introduces no extra mathematical choice. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/DirectSum.lean#L77) passes.
The forward equivalence is precisely the canonical inclusion.
The inverse restores each component of the ambient family.

The equivalence was built from the injective piece inclusion, so forgetting its range proof returns that same inclusion. This agrees with the coordinate action of [Mathlib’s direct-sum map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249). The theorem identifies underlying elements, without claiming the range is the entire ambient direct sum. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/DirectSum.lean#L50) passes.
Each coordinate of the underlying inclusion is the original component.

This is [Mathlib’s direct-sum map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249) applied to the subtype maps Gᵢ(p)→Mᵢ. It preserves each coordinate and finite support, giving an R-linear inclusion for an arbitrary family. The component formula and single-summand formula confirm the exact map. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/DirectSum.lean#L50) passes.
Each coordinate is unchanged after forgetting its membership proof.
Single-summand inputs are sent to the corresponding ambient generator.

[Mathlib’s direct-sum map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249) acts componentwise, so inserting x at i before inclusion equals inserting its underlying element at i afterwards. Both expressions vanish at every other index. The degree and the summand index remain distinct, exactly as the displayed dependent types require. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/DirectSum.lean#L50) passes.
The coordinate formula determines the generator equation.
The resulting ambient generator belongs to the specified degree-p piece.

An ambient element already has finite support. Thus componentwise membership lets it be lifted to a finitely supported family of piece elements, while every included family has that membership. This identifies the range of [Mathlib’s direct-sum map](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249); no additional global finite-support hypothesis is missing. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/DirectSum.lean#L85) passes.
The inverse piece equivalence recovers precisely the ambient coordinates.

The universal map is the finite sum of φᵢ(xᵢ). Each term lies in ℬ(q) by the hypothesis and componentwise membership, and ℬ(q) is additively closed. The direct-sum convention is [Hazrat §1.2.6](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=24); no compatibility between R and S actions is needed for this additive argument. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/Curved/Module/Right/Coproduct.lean#L164) passes.
Actual application: the universal map of curved-module summands changes degree by the prescribed q.

For input degree p, g carries the p+r projection into degree p+r+s and commutes with the corresponding projections. Thus g∘fᵣ=(g∘f)ᵣ₊ₛ. This uses the degree-addition convention of [Stacks 09MN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MN); homogeneity of g is essential, while f may have infinitely many nonzero parts. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/HomogeneousPart.lean#L171) passes.
The complementary precomposition formula checks the order of degree addition.
An already homogeneous map is recovered at its own degree.

On input x=Σp xₚ, the value is Σp πₚ₊ᵣ(f(xₚ)), the component formula in [Hazrat §1.2.3, equation (1.11)](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=23) after reindexing. The input sum is finite, so each selected component is defined without asserting that f has only finitely many nonzero components. The source proves coefficient linearity. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/HomogeneousPart.lean#L86) passes.
A homogeneous input selects exactly the p+r output projection.
Selecting the degree of an already homogeneous map recovers it.

If f has degree r, then f(x) already lies in H(p+r) for every homogeneous x∈G(p). Projection to that piece fixes it, and homogeneous spanning gives equality of maps. This is the recovery property of [Hazrat §1.2.3, equation (1.11)](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=23), with no finite-generation assumption. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/HomogeneousPart.lean#L119) passes.
The converse also holds: being fixed by the selected part implies that degree.

For x in degree p, the defining value is the projection of f(x) to H(p+r), hence lies in that submodule. This is precisely degree-r homogeneity in [Stacks 09MN](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MN). Zero inputs and vanished pieces satisfy membership without assigning a unique degree to zero. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/HomogeneousPart.lean#L119) passes.
The characterization of fixed maps confirms the selected degree convention.

Finite homogeneous expansion in each slot writes the value as a finite sum of homogeneous-tuple values. The hypothesis places each summand in S, whose additive closure gives the conclusion. This matches the finite-support construction in [Mathlib’s dfinsuppFamily](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Multilinear/DFinsupp.lean#L91); no homogeneity of the original map is assumed. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Multilinear/Basic.lean#L69) passes.
Applying the membership criterion to the diagonal yields actual map extensionality.

A homogeneous input has only its p-component, so the defining finite sum collapses to πₚ₊ᵣ(f(x)). This is exactly the specialization of [Hazrat §1.2.3, equation (1.11)](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=23). The input hypothesis is explicit; the formula is not asserted for a general inhomogeneous x. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/HomogeneousPart.lean#L101) passes.
The selected value has the required p+r output degree.

The construction decomposes each input, applies the supplied component map to each degree tuple, and sums. Only finitely many tuples contribute because the slot family and each support are finite, as verified by [Mathlib’s dfinsuppFamily](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Multilinear/DFinsupp.lean#L91). Outputs need no grading or inter-component compatibility. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Multilinear/Basic.lean#L103) passes.
Extension recovers the prescribed value on each homogeneous tuple.
Extending the restrictions of an existing total map recovers it.

For homogeneous inputs, each decomposition is supported at its chosen degree. The single-support computation of [Mathlib’s dfinsuppFamily](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Multilinear/DFinsupp.lean#L91) leaves only that degree tuple, and summing returns f(d)(x). This also covers an empty input family, where there is one empty tuple. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Multilinear/Basic.lean#L112) passes.
The component computation gives the extension/restriction round trip.
The output-degree criterion agrees with the specified component values.

The object is H/ker f, the intermediate Hopf algebra in [Milne, Propositions 3.13–14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). Over the displayed field, the kernel construction’s flatness requirements hold. Published [factorization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L74) and [injective-factor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L109) controls pass. The quotient retains possible nilpotents and is not replaced by a reduced image; the source explicitly leaves scheme-image compatibility separate.
Projection followed by induced factor equals f as a Hopf-algebra morphism.
Kernel quotient factor is injective on coordinate-algebra elements.

This is q:H→H/ker f, the surjective first factor of [Milne, Propositions 3.13–14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). It is an actual Hopf-algebra morphism, not an inclusion of a set-theoretic range. Published [quotient-class evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L79) and [surjectivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L94) controls pass. The orientation is covariant on coordinate algebras and reverses when taking spectra.
Image projection sends x to its quotient class.
Every image-quotient element has a representative.

The lift sends [h] to f(h), the injective second factor in [Milne, Propositions 3.13–14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). Its well-definedness uses the exact ordinary kernel, so no saturation or radical is introduced. Published [representative evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L84) and [injectivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L109) controls pass. The codomain is K, and this map need not be surjective onto K.
The induced factor evaluates [x] as f(x).
Kernel quotient factor is injective on coordinate-algebra elements.

The image projection evaluates as the ordinary quotient class [x], agreeing with [Milne, Propositions 3.13–14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). Both sides land in the same quotient by the Hopf kernel’s underlying ideal. The published [pointwise factorization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L89) passes and sends this class back to f(x). No representative in H is selected from a quotient class.
The pointwise composite sends x to f(x).

The induced map evaluates on [x] as f(x), matching the forward map of [Milne, Propositions 3.13–14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). Two representatives differing by a kernel element have the same value. The published [pointwise factorization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L89) passes. This equality is in K and makes no assertion about an inverse to f or to the inclusion of its image.
The pointwise composite sends x to f(x).

Composing x↦[x] with [x]↦f(x) recovers f(x), exactly the order in [Milne, Propositions 3.13–14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [bundled factorization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L74) passes, checking equality of Hopf morphisms as well as elements. The reverse composite is not asserted; its source and target would differ.
Projection followed by induced factor equals f as a Hopf-algebra morphism.

Every class in H/ker f has a representative, so the first factor is onto as in [Milne, Propositions 3.13–14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). This does not require f itself to be onto K. The published [kernel-preservation consumer](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L124) passes and uses this surjectivity to compare the group-kernel ideals before and after factorization.
Factoring through the ring-kernel quotient preserves the group-kernel ideal.

The quotient has divided out exactly ker f, so its induced map into K is injective, as in [Milne, Propositions 3.13–14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The proof transports through the ordinary kernel quotient, retaining field-level Hopf structure. The published [categorical-monomorphism control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Basic.lean#L132) passes. It asserts injectivity of coordinate-algebra elements, not injectivity or surjectivity on group-scheme points.
Injective induced factor is a categorical monomorphism; actual Prop instance.

The forgetful ideal is the stored carrier itself. Thus the closure laws in [Kytölä’s Hopf-ideal definition](https://math.aalto.fi/~kkytola/files_KK/lectures_files_KK/Hopf-lecture_notes.pdf#page=78) are properties of the original ideal, not a replacement by a radical or generated closure. Published [membership](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Basic.lean#L118) and [counit-kernel](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Augmentation.lean#L113) controls pass. The stored two-sidedness remains available even though Lean’s Ideal type starts with a left ideal.
Underlying ideal and Hopf ideal have exactly the same membership.
The counit-kernel example has precisely the ordinary ideal kernel.

The zero ideal satisfies every law in [Kytölä’s Hopf-ideal definition](https://math.aalto.fi/~kkytola/files_KK/lectures_files_KK/Hopf-lecture_notes.pdf#page=78): comultiplication, counit and antipode send zero to zero, and {0} is two-sided. Published [zero-membership](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Basic.lean#L250) and [full-point-subgroup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L114) controls pass. This is ideal bottom; geometrically it cuts out the whole ambient group, rather than the identity subgroup.
Bottom membership is x=0.
Zero ideal cuts out the full point group over every value algebra.

Forgetting the Hopf structure on bottom returns the ordinary zero ideal, the convention in [Mathlib’s zero submodule](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/Lattice.lean#L49). The published [zero-image](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Map.lean#L179) control passes and uses this equality. The two bottom symbols live in different ordered types but both have carrier {0}; the counit kernel is generally larger.
Ideal extension sends bottom to bottom.

Membership in the zero Hopf ideal is x=0, matching [Mathlib’s zero submodule](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/Lattice.lean#L49). The published [point-subgroup control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L114) passes: every algebra-valued point kills zero, so the subgroup is all points. The equation uses zero in H and does not require H or the base to be nontrivial.
Zero ideal cuts out the full point group over every value algebra.

The zero ideal is below every Hopf ideal because each contains zero, matching [Mathlib’s zero submodule](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/Lattice.lean#L49). The published [image of bottom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Map.lean#L179) and [preimage of bottom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Comap.lean#L147) controls pass. The latter correctly gives ker f, showing that order-bottom structure does not imply every inverse-image operation preserves zero.
Ideal extension sends bottom to bottom.
Preimage of bottom is the Hopf kernel, which may be nonzero.

The binary operation uses I+J. Additivity transports the coideal, counit and antipode laws of [Kytölä’s Hopf-ideal definition](https://math.aalto.fi/~kkytola/files_KK/lectures_files_KK/Hopf-lecture_notes.pdf#page=78), while right multiplication distributes over the sum to retain two-sidedness. The published [sum-membership](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Basic.lean#L306) and [point-intersection](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L128) controls pass. The carrier is not merely I∪J, and no additive inverses are required.
Binary join membership is an additive decomposition into two members.
Binary join cuts out the intersection of the two subgroups over every value algebra.

The underlying ideal of the Hopf join is exactly the ideal sum, agreeing with [Mathlib’s sum membership](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Span/Defs.lean#L381). The published [extension-preserves-join](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Map.lean#L194) control passes with both image two-sidedness assumptions explicit. No extra Hopf closure enlarges the ordinary sum, and the result applies over semirings without a quotient-ring construction.
Image preserves binary joins with both two-sidedness instances retained.

Membership means x=y+z with y∈I and z∈J, exactly [Mathlib’s sum membership](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Span/Defs.lean#L381). It is not the disjunction x∈I or x∈J. The published [all-value-algebra intersection control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L128) passes and uses this decomposition: a point vanishing on both summands vanishes on their sum. Semiring hypotheses suffice.
Binary join cuts out the intersection of the two subgroups over every value algebra.
